Sentence (English): Overall I am happy with this 800 series and would recommend it.
Comments (English): [ Dependable performance, few drawbacks ] || ---------------- || Overall I am happy with this 800 series and would recommend it. To start with the pros, the most important thing is that it does what it says on the tin, which is to wash dishes. I can say unequivocally that this dishwasher gets my dishes cleaner than any other I've had. Drying performance is excellent and as advertised, but make sure to 1) use crystal dry and 2) enable "intensive drying" in the settings. I was disappointed at first that this model doesn't open the door at the end of drying to let the moisture evaporate, but after using it for a couple months I can say it's unnecessary. Sure, some water on concave surfaces might collect, but other than that my dishes come out nice and dry, even plasticware. I was also concerned that there is only one utensil basket, but the top rack is so much nicer that sometimes I don't bother putting the basket in at all. I like that the machine is quiet and energy/water efficient. It looks nice in the kitchen. It's easy to maintain. The cons are minor, but in my opinion worth docking a star for. First, since it's a top control unit, it's impossible to know how much time is left while a cycle is running, since the door is closed. It's frustrating that this model doesn't have the remaining time projected down to the floor, even at this price. The info light is marginally useful, if the kitchen is quiet you can obviously hear it running, if it's noisy maybe not. Speaking of top controls, the capacitive touch buttons are a significant downgrade from physical buttons, since they are easy to activate on accident. Several options and features are impossible to use with the top controls, and require the app instead. I will say that the app is the most useful among a general crowd of useless appliance apps, which of course isn't saying much, but I don't mind using it, which I suppose is saying something. Another thing I dislike is the general feeling of flimsiness of the door and racks. It just doesn't feel solid at all, in contrast to the nice stainless look and feel. The door's hinges allow quite a bit of torsion (open the door, put a hand on either side of the door, and move your hands in opposite directions), which even a heavy oven door will allow but here it feels cheap and finicky, as if you always need to hold and press exactly in the center of the door/handle. Bosch says the rack glide system is newly redesigned, but all that indicates to me is that it must have been in a sorry state indeed if this is the improved version. It doesn't feel sturdy or smooth, and is hardly different from the cheap Samsung this unit replaced. Again, I recommend this unit on wash performance alone. A KitchenAid might be cheaper but I'd doubt the dishes come out as clean and dry as the Bosch. Maybe the build quality and some features are better on other brands, but I have a hard time believing my dishes could come out any cleaner than the 800 makes them.

Sentence (English): Lowes Customer service was not helpful.
Comments (English): Lowes Customer service was not helpful. They told me I had to contact whirlpool and it is not their problem. Whirlpool has ignored my emails. This means I will have to use time I should be working to call them during business hours. Yeah! a part time job just to get something fixed that I already paid for. The dishwasher I just purchased has been leaking when it is running ever since being installed. It took me a few days to identify where it was coming from. It is from the seam of the tub on the left side near the front. The drips just barely miss the catch tray that is supposed to divert the leak to the leak detection sensor. Sometimes the leak also runs down the support foot. I now have the bottom skirt off and a pan under that foot of the dishwasher to keep the water from ruining the floor and cabinets. Beside the leak, it washes fine and I like the arrangement of the racks. Super disappointed in Lowes stance on this obvious defect.

Sentence (English): I had a Samsung 6-seater, but the moving company broke it.
Comments (English): I had a Samsung 6-seater, but the moving company broke it. However, since there was a mini monitor mounted in the kitchen where it was supposed to be installed, the height didn't fit. So I got rid of it and looked for a new one. My criteria were white, clean, not too big, and with a two-tier interior. After looking around, I found this was the only one that fit. I was worried because it wasn't a domestic product, but someone told me this one was a good value for money since all the systems were similar. I took it to the after-sales service center, and it was probably defective, so they refunded me. I bought a new one for a bit more than the previous one, but the other one got stuck on the top and couldn't be installed anyway. I had no other choice. Then, I think they upgraded it. My old one didn't have a blade under the second tier, but now it has a rotating blade that dispenses water. It'll wash cups even better. It cleans well, doesn't leave many water marks, removes dirt cleanly, feels smooth to the touch, and dries just as well as the previous one. It's a good value for the money. The exterior is neat and square, so it doesn't look stuffy when placed on the countertop, and I'm satisfied with the cleanliness.
